n3-private.meaning_mnemonic: A stalk of <radical>grain</radical> leans over on the left, and tucked in behind it on the right is a little <radical>cocoon</radical>, sealed tight. Nobody else knows it is there. You grew the whole crop out in the open, then wrapped one seed away for yourself and told no one. Grain kept back inside a cocoon is what is <radical>private</radical>.
n3-private.reading_mnemonic: Shi is the quiet one who keeps her own small field behind the house, and when anyone asks what she is growing in it she says 「<reading>し</reading>」 and closes the gate. Not rude, exactly. Whatever is in there is hers, and し is the only answer you are ever going to get.

n3-what.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>person</radical> stands at the left with a line in his hand — you can see the <radical>barb</radical> at the end of it, and a flat bar of <radical>ground</radical> above the open <radical>mouth</radical> below. He has hooked something out of the water and hauled it up, and now he is just staring at it with his mouth hanging open, because he has no idea <radical>what</radical> it is.
n3-what.reading_mnemonic: Kaa the fire-breathing crow drops onto the power line above him and looks at the thing on the hook. She has never seen one either. All she manages is one puzzled croak — 「<reading>か</reading>?」 — with a little puff of flame behind it. か? か? Neither of them knows.

n3-morning.meaning_mnemonic: The <radical>sun</radical> is caught low in a <radical>cross</radical>-braced frame on the left, still climbing, while over on the right the <radical>moon</radical> has not gone down yet. Both of them are up there at once. That happens for about twenty minutes a day, and only ever at one end of it: <radical>morning</radical>.
n3-morning.reading_mnemonic: Chou is the long-distance runner who is out before anybody else, and she stretches her greeting the whole length of the street as she passes your window — a long, unreasonably cheerful 「<reading>ちょう</reading>」. If you hear ちょう, the moon is still up.

n3-daytime.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>body</radical> is slumped across the top with a single <radical>drop</radical> of sweat coming off it, and directly underneath sits the <radical>sun</radical>, pinned against a flat line of <radical>ground</radical>. It is straight overhead and there is no shade left anywhere. Work has stopped and everyone has lain down. This is the flattening middle of the <radical>daytime</radical>.
n3-daytime.reading_mnemonic: Chuu the loyal mouse will not nap through it. While every other body is flat out he stands at his post in the full sun, squeaking 「<reading>ちゅう</reading>」 on the hour so that nobody oversleeps. Absurdly devoted, ちゅう, right through the worst of it.

n3-evening.meaning_mnemonic: Three strokes and nothing else: a curve like the shoulder of a hill, with one line falling through it. It is the moon, only half up and not yet bright, caught at the exact moment the light goes flat and blue and everything loses its edges. Nothing has happened yet. The whole character is one picture of <radical>evening</radical> starting.
n3-evening.reading_mnemonic: Seki comes out onto his step at this hour every night, and you hear him before you see him — that wet, rattling 「<reading>せき</reading>」 of a cough carrying right down the street. When せき starts up, the light has gone.

n3-night.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>lid</radical> is pulled across the top of the sky, and a <radical>person</radical> slips underneath it just as the last of the <radical>evening</radical> drains away. Once that lid is on, nothing more gets in — no sun, no colour, nobody else. The lid down over the evening, with somebody still out under it: <radical>night</radical>.
n3-night.reading_mnemonic: Ya is the yakitori man who only opens once the lid is down. The cart comes out of nowhere, the lantern goes up, and he calls one syllable into the dark — 「<reading>や</reading>」 — which is the entire advertisement. If you can hear や, it is night.

n3-gone.meaning_mnemonic: A mound of <radical>earth</radical> on top, and underneath it that little sealed <radical>cocoon</radical>, tucked well out of sight. Whatever was inside wrapped itself up, went under the soil, and never came back out. You can dig the whole mound over and there is nothing left in there to find. It is <radical>gone</radical>.
n3-gone.reading_mnemonic: Kyo is the magician who buries things and cannot get them back. He taps the mound, says 「<reading>きょ</reading>」 with a flourish, and that is genuinely the end of the trick. No reappearance, no second half. きょ, and it is gone.

n3-father.meaning_mnemonic: Two arms crossing over each other at the top, two legs braced wide underneath. It is a stance, not a face — the shape of a man standing square in a doorway with his arms folded, filling the whole frame, waiting to hear what you have got to say for yourself. Everybody recognises that silhouette: <radical>father</radical>.
n3-father.reading_mnemonic: Fu is the long breath out through the nose that he gives you instead of an answer — 「<reading>ふ</reading>」 — arms still folded. Not angry. Not pleased either. Just ふ, and you will be hearing it for the rest of your life.

n3-mother.meaning_mnemonic: A figure kneeling with her arms wrapped round in front of her, and two dots marking the breasts that fed you. The entire character is built around those two points; take them out and it turns into a different word altogether. They are the reason the shape exists at all, and the reason you call her <radical>mother</radical>.
n3-mother.reading_mnemonic: Bo is the one syllable a baby manages long before it manages anything else — 「<reading>ぼ</reading>」 — blown out with a bubble of spit and aimed straight at whoever is holding it. She answers to ぼ years before she answers to her own name.

n3-friend.meaning_mnemonic: One stroke <radical>slides</radical> down from the top left across a bar of <radical>ground</radical>, and underneath it a <radical>right hand</radical> comes up to meet it. Two hands reaching in from opposite directions and closing on each other. Nobody is being paid for this and nobody is in charge of anybody. That is a <radical>friend</radical>.
n3-friend.reading_mnemonic: Yuu is the one who is always there before you, hand already out, drawing the greeting into a long two-beat call across the car park — 「<reading>ゆう</reading>」 — before you have even shut the car door. ゆう means somebody is glad to see you.

n3-doctor.meaning_mnemonic: A <radical>box on its side</radical>, its open mouth turned towards you, and lying inside it an <radical>arrow</radical> — the one they have just drawn out of you, dropped in the tray. The lid comes down over the arrowhead and the wound both. Whoever owns that box and knows what to do with what comes out of you is the <radical>doctor</radical>.
n3-doctor.reading_mnemonic: Ii is the noise she makes while examining you: one short noncommittal 「<reading>い</reading>」 as she looks at the wound, and another as she drops the arrow into the tray. Nothing whatsoever about い tells you whether it is bad news.
